1.why: MFA routes go through owner(), which requires a valid session in stage mfa whose userId matches the signed-in ACCOUNT.id.

2.why: Verification material is bound to the caller session (per-session identity hash, pending TOTP secret, and backup hashes), so the same code does not authorize a different user/session.

3.why: Enabling MFA only mutates the current session (o.enabled/o.enrolled); no code invalidates other existing sessions, so prior sessions continue to work.

4.why: Pending/enrolled OTP secrets are stored with AES-GCM encrypt(), and backup codes are stored as peppered SHA-256 hashes, not plaintext.

5.why: token(), secret(), codes(), and related helpers use crypto.getRandomValues (CSPRNG); fixed values appear only in explicit TEST mode.

6.why: Session id is only in an HttpOnly cookie; client code does not write secrets/OTPs/tokens to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, password, OTP, and recovery inputs via bounded length checks and strict regex/format helpers before use.

8.why: UI rendering escapes untrusted strings with the e() HTML encoder, and CSP nonce restricts script execution.

9.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist (only location.reload and static responses), so open redirects are avoided even without an explicit redirect allow-list.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: secureCookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Production error handler returns a generic 500 without stack traces and secrets are not put in URLs; TEST-only client logs can expose codes when test mode is on.

13.why: Identity codes expire (LIFE) and are cleared after success; backup codes are removed on use; TOTP is time-bound though not recorded as single-use within its window.

14.why: identity/otp/recovery failures increment counters and lock for LOCK after MAX attempts, returning 429 while locked.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a new id; get() enforces idle/absolute timeouts; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
